rounds.reason: The whole five-card lock wave was vetoed for the same defect: the sealed acceptance oracle held only three generic structural checks (a schema line, the presence of any sha256-shaped string, and the absence of a mutable-reference token) and never parsed the lock's fields. Both of this card's Skeptical Mutations passed silently at exit 0 -- mutating the module path or deleting a per-module checksum produced no failure. The builder delivered real, source-traceable lock content and disclosed the gap in docs/specs/AUR-360.md rather than hiding it; the defect was in the oracle, not the content.

rounds.governance_change: No card-spec change. The oracle was rewritten to cross-check the lock against the real go.mod and go.sum field by field, as a bijection in both directions, and the eleven cases.tsv fixtures are now actually executed by a self-test loop instead of merely shipped.
rounds.candidate: r2 patch applied against base_sha 7a1b93024842aa889e3e9820c1b4bcb5c55a9dc3; integrated by the coordinator as a staged working tree at bundle time.

note: This bundle proves round 2 against the current candidate_identity_digest, with three independent seals over the same candidate: the adversarial reviewer and blind reviewers A and B, all reproducing RED, GREEN (stdout sha256 b71d3f62...) and both card mutations from scratch. A non-blocking contract tension is recorded by all three: the card's Public contract enumerates four typed codes while MUT-001/MUT-002 name two others literally, and .board/cards is forbidden_paths for this card, so the reconciliation belongs to a future governance card rather than to this candidate.
